title: The Teaching Example: 99 Ordinary Emails vs. 1 Spam
text: Ask two questions. How many labels are correct overall and how many actual spam emails are caught? Imagine 100 emails, 99 ordinary emails and one spam email. These are made up teaching counts, not measurements of a real inbox. Our classifier always says ordinary. It labels the 99 ordinary emails correctly and misses the spam. That's 99 correct labels out of 100, 99% accuracy.

title: Calculating Overall Accuracy vs. Spam Recall
text: Now show the missed spam beside the overall score. Of the one spam email, our rule catches zero. Spam recall asks what fraction of the actual spam was caught. Here it's zero out of one or zero percent. The high accuracy came from getting the common category right. It did not show that the rule could detect spam.
